title: Gift Budget Pair
statement: An online shop lists 2,000,000 gift prices sorted from cheapest to most expensive. A customer with a gift card wants two different gifts that use the card's exact value.
constraints: Memory is tight: no second copy of the prices

approaches.name: Two pointers from both ends, moving the one that fixes the sum
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: The sorted order tells which pointer may move; nothing is checked twice and no extra memory is used.

approaches.name: One pass with a hash set of prices seen so far
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Also linear, but it stores up to 2,000,000 prices, which the memory limit rules out.

approaches.name: For each price, binary search for its partner
approaches.hint: Search the rest of the list
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct and uses no extra memory, but slower than one pass.

title: Cleaning a Sensor Log
statement: A sensor writes 10,000,000 readings into an array; a reading of -1 means a failed measurement. The device has no room for a second array and must drop the failed readings while keeping the rest in order.

approaches.name: A read pointer over every reading and a write pointer for the next kept one
approaches.hint: Pack the good ones at the front
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: One pass, order kept, and only two indexes of extra memory.

approaches.name: Copy the good readings into a new array
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct and simple, but it needs a second array that the device does not have room for.

approaches.name: Delete each -1 from the array as soon as it is found
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Each deletion shifts every later reading, which is slow with many failures.

approaches.name: Sort the readings so the -1s come first, then skip them
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: It loses the original order of the readings.

title: Two Sorted Playlists
statement: Two music services each send a playlist of track IDs sorted ascending, 500,000 tracks each. The app needs the tracks that appear in both lists.

approaches.name: Walk both lists with one pointer each, moving the pointer at the smaller ID
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Each step moves at least one pointer, and the output comes out sorted.

approaches.name: Put one list in a hash set and look up the other
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Also linear, but it ignores that both lists are sorted and stores 500,000 IDs.

approaches.name: For each ID in one list, binary search the other
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, a little slower than one walk.

approaches.name: Compare every ID with every other ID
approaches.label: unsuitable
